 Advertisement Cornell High School football coach dies after medical emergency at game
 Cornell head coach Ed Dawson dies at hospital after medics respond to sideline at Rochester football field in Beaver County
 Advertisement Updated: 11:15 AM EDT Oct 24, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Cornell High School football coach dies after medical emergency at game
 Cornell head coach Ed Dawson dies at hospital after medics respond to sideline at Rochester football field in Beaver County
 Updated: 11:15 AM EDT Oct 24, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ ROCHESTER, Pa. — Cornell High School football coach Ed Dawson died after a medical emergency during the team's game Friday night, the district superintendent said.
 "I am extremely saddened and shocked to report that Coach Dawson has passed away," Superintendent Aaron Thomas said in a statement.
 Advertisement The Cornell Raiders were playing Rochester. Beaver County emergency dispatchers confirmed that medics responded to the sideline at the Rochester football field.
 No additional details regarding the nature of the medical emergency were immediately released. 
 This is a developing story. Stay with Pittsburgh's Action News 4 for updates. 
 TribLIVE Cornell High School football coach Ed Dawson at a team practice in August 2025 Statement from Cornell School District Superintendent Aaron Thomas
 We want to update everyone on a situation that happened at the away football game this evening at Rochester High School. During the game Head Football Coach Ed Dawson experienced a medical emergency and was transported to a local hospital. I am extremely saddened and shocked to report that Coach Dawson has passed away.
 This is an extremely difficult situation. To say Coach Dawson was an integral part of Cornell School District would be an understatement. It is hard to put into words what Coach Dawson means to Cornell and we are all heart broken, crushed, and in shock. We will work to ensure our students and staff have the resources they need and right now our thoughts and prayers are with Coach Dawson and his family. We have difficult days ahead and we will lean on each other to get through them the best we can. We love you Coach Dawson.
 Statement from Coraopolis Mayor Michael Dixon
 Tonight our community lost one of its giants. Coach Ed Dawson passed away this evening, and the Borough of Coraopolis joins Cornell School District, his players, and his family in heartbreak.
 When Cornell stepped away from football in 2012, a lot of people assumed Friday nights here were over. Coach Dawson didn't accept that. When the Raiders returned in 2016, he started with a few dozen kids and a lot of faith.
 They lost their first 18 games and kept showing up anyway, even at youth league games, making sure every young person in this town knew there was a place for them on his team.
 By 2019, he had led the Raiders to their first section title in 36 years, the first WPIAL playoff win in school history, and the WPIAL semifinals. He took them back to the semifinals in 2021.
 The wins mattered. The young men he shaped mattered more. Coach Dawson looked for the positive in every game and in every kid, and he taught them to sweat the details and never quit. Generations of Cornell and Nazareth Prep players grew into better men because he believed in them before they believed in themselves.
 To Coach Dawson's family: Coraopolis grieves with you, and we will stand beside you in the days ahead. To his players and coaching staff: lean on each other and on this community. You were his team, and you are ours.
 Thank you, Coach. We love you, and we will not forget what you built here.
